x: Wes Smith had flown in from Finland at midnight yet still won the B while James Everard nipped past him in the last round to get a good third in the A javelin.
A similar scenario unfolded in the javelin where both James Everard and Wes Smith threw further than in match one but were rewarded with fewer points.

Wes Smith and James Everard outgunned the Newham lads in the javelin and we were away. We welcomed Samson Oni back for the high jump after injury and although he narrowly missed 2.20 his 2.15 clearance was good enough for second in the A competition while the ubiquitous Sempers added more points, fi…

…nce last August, the throwers were adding significantly to our points tally; and then two 2nds came in the Javelin with Wes Smith (pictured above by Jeremy Hemming) throwing two pb’s to just pip Tom Dobbing in the last round.…
Then the B results: Wes Smith was second (10 points) with Sam Ellis of Sheffield third (8 points).

James had a knee operation seven weeks ago and his colleague in the javelin – Wes Smith – had had a similar operation just four weeks ago. Nonetheless they contributed 12 points and we were home and dry.

And our final debutant for the season was Wes Smith who 11 months ago broke his arm while throwing the javelin. Now recovered from surgery Wes flew in from Finland for his first competition since the accident and tentatively threw just under 53m to back up James Everard who gained a useful fourth in the A javelin.
